issues.label: Two-step due process identification test
issues.why: Court must apply Kaneaiakala's framework of assessing suggestiveness first, then reliability under totality of circumstances.

issues.label: Whether show-up was impermissibly suggestive
issues.why: Handcuffs, solo presentation, officer standing behind, and 'in custody' statements bear on suggestiveness.

issues.label: Failure to give may-or-may-not-be-present warning
issues.why: Officers admittedly could not warn CW that perpetrator might not be in the show-up, a HAWJIC 3.19A factor.

issues.label: Circuit court's omission of HAWJIC 3.19A factors
issues.why: Central question is whether the court erred by analyzing only 3.19 reliability factors and not 3.19A suggestiveness factors.

issues.label: Whether express factor-by-factor findings are required
issues.why: State questions whether the court must expressly address each 3.19A factor in its ruling.

issues.label: Whether court in fact considered suggestiveness
issues.why: State contends the court implicitly weighed suggestiveness despite not listing 3.19A factors.

issues.label: Reliability notwithstanding suggestiveness
issues.why: Court must determine whether identification reliability outweighs the suggestive procedure's taint.

issues.label: Language barrier's effect on identification
issues.why: CW's Chuukese primary language and absence of interpreter/warning may have compromised the identification process.

issues.label: Absence of interpreter during show-up
issues.why: CW was transported without her granddaughter or a Chuukese translator, affecting instructions and understanding.

issues.label: Opportunity to observe / stress factors
issues.why: CW's brief violent encounter and stress at time of observation affect reliability under HAWJIC 3.19.

issues.label: Cross-racial/ethnic identification concerns
issues.why: Potential cross-ethnic nature of identification is an enumerated reliability factor requiring consideration.

issues.label: Adequacy of prior description
issues.why: Only a brief verbal description was given via granddaughter; fit with defendant bears on reliability.

issues.label: Time between crime and identification
issues.why: The short interval and geographic proximity of bus stop are relevant reliability factors.

issues.label: Break in chase / possible misidentification
issues.why: Hernandez lost sight of suspect 10-15 seconds and Wainit lacked clear view, raising wrong-person risk.

issues.label: Witness certainty and its foundation
issues.why: CW's stated certainty based on face must be weighed for whether it is well-founded.

issues.label: Standard of review on appeal
issues.why: Court must identify correct standard for reviewing admissibility of identification evidence.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: State argues any identification error was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt given other evidence.

issues.label: Proper remedy: suppression versus new trial
issues.why: ICA remanded without indicating admissibility, requiring clarification of the correct disposition.

issues.label: Burden of proof on identification reliability
issues.why: Court must determine which party bears the burden regarding show-up reliability/suggestiveness.

issues.label: HRS 707-711(1)(m) elements and victim age
issues.why: Second-degree assault charge premised on victim being 60+ requires identity proof beyond reasonable doubt.
